ground_truth.description: The single-task check is instructed to use search(..., limit=50) and to rely on the vector-ranking bias from appending 'task_id=<N>' to the query to surface the one target record. On a busy project with more than ~50 'stage1_flag_suppression' records, embeddings do not reliably rank an exact task_id token match into the top 50 (numeric task_id tokens are weakly discriminated by the embedding, and the dominant term 'stage1_flag_suppression' is shared by every record), so the authoritative suppression record can fall below the cutoff and be missed. The reader then concludes 'no suppression in effect' and emits a flag that should have been suppressed — exactly the false-negative (review-passed-but-escalation-created) failure this task was flagged for. The post-processor's own sweep uses limit=501 precisely to avoid this; capping the reader's check at 50 reintroduces the miss.

On search error/timeout the prompt directs the reader to treat suppression as not-in-effect and emit the flag (fail-open with respect to suppression). It justifies this as mirroring filter_suppressed's 'conservative pass-through', but pass-through in the post-processor keeps flags for the opposite reason; here it means an intentionally suppressed task can get a flag emitted on a transient search failure, which is the same false-negative direction and relies entirely on the downstream post-processor still catching it.

provenance.runs_db_query: SELECT task_id, project_id, outcome, review_cycles, verify_attempts FROM task_results WHERE review_cycles >= 1, cross-referenced with events (escalation_created, merge_finalized) -- see mining.mine_fn_candidates.
